author: WP04
summary: Teaches the math conventions (right-handed basis, row vectors, application-order products, [0,1] depth, clip-space W, ToColumnMajor), the vector/matrix/quaternion operation groups, bounding-volume and curve boundaries, Color packing and degenerate-input policy. The alpha.1-era text predates the XNA oracles, the ties-to-even colour rounding and XNA-IL comparisons; several stated defects are narrower or broader than written (frustum ray, curve Step). libcna.com already had deep maintainer internals and member tables; the XNA-behaviour comparison, conventions and degenerate-input semantics went into six framework deep dives.

concepts.text: CNA's math values connect game code, content, effects and renderers; the names follow XNA, but correct use depends on conventions the method names do not reveal: row-vector composition, a right-handed basis, packed colour layout, interval boundaries and several incomplete geometric paths.
tokens: the names do not say which way the axes point

concepts.text: The public headers under modules/math/include are the signature authority; a compact API inventory lives elsewhere (the site's member tables are the Math types guide and the public header index).
concepts.note: Book-navigation sentence; the site equivalent is docs/math-types.html and development/reference/public-headers.html.

concepts.text: Apart from BoundingFrustum (and Curve/CurveKeyCollection, which own a vector of keys), the core math types are C++ value types with public fields: copying copies the value, with no identity, heap ownership or disposal.
concepts.note: Bible names only BoundingFrustum as the exception; Curve owns its CurveKeyCollection by value, which holds a std::vector of CurveKey.

concepts.text: BoundingFrustum is a class that stores its matrix and caches six derived planes and eight corners; setMatrixProperty recomputes both, and equality/hash use only the matrix.
tokens: caches six planes and eight corners

concepts.text: Most arithmetic families have two spellings: a value-returning form and an output-reference form with a trailing result& that mirrors XNA's ref/out overloads.
The value-returning and output-reference forms are separate public declarations (tested separately; the value form usually delegates).

An output-reference form is not necessarily alias-safe: Matrix::Transpose(m, m) writes result fields while still reading the source and symmetrises the matrix; Plane::Transform uses exactly that call. Most other out-forms (Multiply, Invert, transforms, Cross, quaternion products) read into locals first and are alias-safe.
concepts.note: Bible's general warning narrowed: at TARGET Transpose is the alias-unsafe out-form; XNA's own Transpose(ref,out) is alias-safe.

target.evidence: modules/math/src/Matrix.cpp (Transpose, Multiply, Invert); modules/math/src/Plane.cpp (Transform); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework assembly (decompiled, xna4-decomp; not a CNA file) (Matrix.Transpose ref/out copies to locals)

concepts.text: Default construction yields XNA's default(T): a zero Matrix (not the identity) and a zero Quaternion (not a rotation); identity comes from Matrix::getIdentityProperty() (a function-local static) or Quaternion::Identity.
concepts.note: TARGET extension of the mental model.

concepts.text: Vectors, matrices, quaternions, planes, rays, Point/Rectangle, the bounding volumes and CurveKey expose equality and hashing, and most expose ToString; equality is exact float comparison with no epsilon, plus Equals(std::any) for XNA's Equals(object).

Hash return types are not uniform (int for vectors, Matrix and Quaternion; intcs for Point and Rectangle; std::size_t for Plane, Ray, Color, CurveKey and the bounding volumes); abstract over them with auto or a normalised hash type.

CNA hash values are not XNA's integers, and the vector/matrix/quaternion/curve-key hashes use raw float bits, so -0.0f and +0.0f components compare equal but hash differently (.NET Single.GetHashCode returns 0 for both zeros).
concepts.note: TARGET extension; recorded as issue WP04-i010.

concepts.text: ToString follows XNA's shapes (Matrix reproduces XNA's exact outer braces), but Ray and BoundingBox print literal doubled braces copied from FNA's concatenation, and numbers use std::ostringstream defaults rather than .NET culture formatting.
concepts.note: TARGET extension; issues WP04-i008, i009.

concepts.text: Private debugger-display helpers and CheckForNaNs (vectors always throw std::logic_error; Matrix/Quaternion only without NDEBUG) have no call site, so they have no runtime effect.
concepts.note: True for the private helpers; Color::getDebugDisplayStringProperty is public CNAEXT and is called by the C ABI (B1, CNA-BUG-042 NOT A BUG). Also stated on the numerics deep dive.

concepts.text: Vector3::Forward is (0,0,-1) and Backward (0,0,1): CNA uses XNA's right-handed world basis, with no left-handed builder variants.
CNA uses row-vector transforms: a position multiplies the matrix from the left (p' = pM), translation lives in M41-M43 and Vector3::Transform never reads the fourth column.
tokens: the fourth column (M14, M24, M34, M44) is never read

concepts.text: Matrix products read in application order: Multiply(a, b) applies a first, so rotation * translation rotates first and translates second; a worked point shows spin*move vs move*spin.
tokens: the left operand is applied first

concepts.text: The standard vertex path is p_clip = p_object * World * View * Projection, and the usual world matrix is scale * rotation * translation; OpenGL's column-vector chain is its transpose.
Perspective clip space needs four components; W must be preserved until clipping and the perspective divide have completed.
The public depth convention is [0, 1] (Direct3D): the projection builders map -near to 0 and -far to 1.

A renderer may translate the depth convention for its native API while application matrices and effects stay XNA-shaped: CNA's GL stock shaders append gl_Position.z = gl_Position.z * 2.0 - gl_Position.w, matching MojoShader's conversion for compiled effects.
tokens: Application matrices and effect parameters stay XNA-shaped
concepts.note: Extended with the concrete TARGET mechanism.

concepts.text: Vector2, Vector3 and Vector4 provide public components, zero/one/unit constants, arithmetic, dot products, distances, normalisation, reflection, clamping and the XNA interpolation family.
Vector3 adds the direction constants and Cross; Vector4::Transform accepts Vector2, Vector3 or Vector4 inputs and returns all four clip components.
tokens: accepts a Vector2, Vector3 or Vector4

concepts.text: Lerp (and Barycentric, CatmullRom, Hermite) take the amount as given, so an amount outside [0, 1] extrapolates.
Normalising a zero vector divides by zero: 1/sqrt(0) is infinite and every component becomes NaN; CNA substitutes no fallback direction.
Validate input where non-finite output would escape into gameplay or rendering; the guarded move-toward example never normalises a zero vector and never overshoots.

Cross-product order sets the normal's sign: for a triangle (a, b, c), Cross(b - a, c - a) reverses when b and c are exchanged, and the same winding controls face culling (default CullCounterClockwise).
tokens: exchanging b and c reverses both the normal and the culling decision

concepts.text: Arithmetic group: Add, Subtract, component/scalar Multiply and Divide, Negate, operators, Min, Max and Clamp; scalar division divides each component whereas XNA multiplies by one reciprocal, and Vector3::operator/= alone uses the reciprocal.
concepts.note: TARGET extension on the Bible's list; issue WP04-i001.

concepts.text: Vector Clamp lets max win on an inverted range and vector/scalar Min/Max pick different operands for NaN than XNA; MathHelper::Clamp matches XNA.
concepts.note: Published by B1 as CNA-BUG-027; stated here as a plain scoped fact.

concepts.text: Measurement group: Length, LengthSquared, Distance, DistanceSquared and Dot, plus Vector3::Cross; Vector3's length and distance are summed in float although CNA measured XNA accumulating them wider.
tokens: length and distance are summed in

concepts.text: Interpolation group: Lerp, SmoothStep, Barycentric, CatmullRom and Hermite; amounts are caller-controlled except that SmoothStep clamps its amount to [0, 1] first.
tokens: SmoothStep clamps its amount to [0, 1] first
concepts.note: The Bible says amounts are caller-controlled for the whole group; SmoothStep clamps.

concepts.text: Transforms group: matrix and quaternion Transform plus array/range forms (std::out_of_range on bad ranges); TransformNormal omits translation and exists for Vector2 and Vector3 only.
tokens: exists on Vector2 and Vector3 only

concepts.text: TransformNormal multiplies by the matrix itself, not its inverse transpose, so normals stay perpendicular only under rotation and uniform scale.
concepts.note: TARGET extension.

concepts.text: Vector3::Transform(position, projection) returns three components without w and without the divide, so it cannot feed a software rasteriser or a manual clipping stage for perspective projections.
tokens: without its w and without dividing by it

concepts.text: Vector4::Transform returns w = x·M14 + y·M24 + z·M34 + M44 and leaves the perspective divide to the caller.
tokens: the divide is left to the caller

concepts.text: The Software renderer transforms with Vector4::Transform, clips in clip space against the 0..w volume and divides only afterwards.
The clip snippet is illustrative: production code must handle the clip volume and the sign and magnitude of W (a point behind the eye has negative w).
tokens: a point behind the camera has negative w

concepts.text: Vector3::Transform is accumulated in double and narrowed once (XNA x87 reproduction) while Vector4::Transform is plain single precision.
concepts.note: TARGET extension.

concepts.text: Matrix stores sixteen public float fields M11-M44 in row order; translation is row four and the direction accessors read the first three rows (Right, Up, Backward; Forward/Down/Left negated).
The principal factory groups are translation, scale, rotations, quaternion conversion, look-at/world, orthographic and perspective projections, billboards, planar shadow and reflection.
All angles are radians; MathHelper::ToRadians and ToDegrees are the only degree-aware functions.
tokens: Every angle parameter in the module is in radians

concepts.text: Object-transform factories: CreateTranslation, CreateScale, CreateRotationX/Y/Z, CreateFromAxisAngle, CreateFromQuaternion and CreateFromYawPitchRoll.

Camera/projection factories: CreateLookAt, CreateWorld, CreateOrthographic(OffCenter) and CreatePerspective*; LookAt's backward axis is position - target and the builders' exact terms are traced for maintainers.

Special-geometry factories: CreateBillboard, CreateConstrainedBillboard, CreateShadow and CreateReflection; CreateBillboard guards coincident object and camera positions (squared distance below 0.0001) as XNA does, but not a parallel up vector.
tokens: Matrix::CreateBillboard with object and camera at the same point
concepts.note: Extended with the degenerate-input guard.

concepts.text: Algebra: Add, Subtract, matrix/scalar Multiply and Divide, Negate, Invert, Transpose and component-wise Lerp; the scalar-left operator*(float, Matrix) is genuine XNA API and operator*= is CNAEXT.
Matrix::Lerp interpolates all sixteen fields; it is not a substitute for decomposing a transform and interpolating the rotation with Quaternion::Slerp.
tokens: not a substitute for decomposing two transforms

concepts.text: Matrix::Invert does not report a singular input; a zero determinant yields infinities and NaNs, so callers need their own validity check (Determinant()).
Decompose(scale, rotation, translation) returns false when any recovered axis scale is near zero and sets rotation to identity; scale and translation remain valid.
tokens: Returns false with rotation set to Quaternion::Identity
concepts.note: The sign-of-zero history is preserved on the math internals page (#decompose).

concepts.text: CNAEXT Matrix::ToColumnMajor(float[16]) copies the sixteen fields in declaration order; it performs no numeric transpose.

The bridge relies on the receiving shader API reading the bytes as column-major storage, so GL column i equals CNA/HLSL row i and M*v in GLSL equals v*M on the CPU; the stock effects call it at the upload boundary.
tokens: sees column i equal to CNA's row i

concepts.text: The dedicated test uses the identity matrix, which cannot distinguish a copy from a transpose; renderer code and non-identity output are the evidence for the convention.
Do not transpose or swap near/far terms in shared math to fix one renderer; inspect that renderer's upload and clip-space translation first.
concepts.note: Also on the math internals page.

concepts.text: Quaternion provides axis-angle, rotation-matrix and yaw/pitch/roll construction, normalisation, conjugate and inverse, arithmetic, Lerp and Slerp.
CreateFromYawPitchRoll expands to q_yaw * q_pitch * q_roll: a vector is rolled (Z), then pitched (X), then yawed (Y) about fixed axes, and Matrix::CreateFromYawPitchRoll delegates to the quaternion.
concepts.note: TARGET extension (derived term by term).

concepts.text: Quaternion multiplication reads backwards relative to Matrix: q1 * q2 applies q2's rotation first, then q1's; CreateFromQuaternion(q1*q2) equals CreateFromQuaternion(q2)*CreateFromQuaternion(q1).
Quaternion::Concatenate(a, b) promises a followed by b and is term for term the product b * a; use it when the call site should read in rotation order.
tokens: term for term the product value2 * value1

concepts.text: Quaternion::Lerp chooses the short arc (negating the second input for a negative dot), mixes components linearly and normalises the result.
tokens: negates the second when the dot is negative

concepts.text: Quaternion::Slerp follows the sphere with uniform angular progress, flips to the shorter arc and falls back to unnormalised linear weights when |dot| exceeds 0.999999; neither Lerp nor Slerp clamps the amount.
For small turns Lerp and Slerp agree; a long slow rotation exposes Lerp's non-uniform (ease-in/ease-out) rate, and feeding a fraction of the remaining angle per frame is an exponential ease.
tokens: visibly speeds up in the middle of the arc

concepts.text: A retained screenshot-infrastructure program compared a Z-axis matrix rotation with the axis-angle quaternion route, and matrix components, transformed point and image agreed at the build used for the artifact.
concepts.note: The program is part of the book repository's own tooling (tools/cna-screenshot-infra), not CNA, and ran against an older CNA revision; it is evidence for that revision only. The equivalence it demonstrated is stated from source on the conventions page (#quaternion-order).

concepts.text: Plane stores a normal and D; DotCoordinate includes D and classifies a point's side, DotNormal tests a direction only.
Ray stores Position and Direction and every intersection returns std::optional<float>; box and plane results are ray parameters, the sphere result a distance only for a unit direction.
BoundingBox, BoundingSphere and BoundingFrustum expose containment and intersection families, whose per-pair behaviour against XNA 4.0 is tabulated.
tokens: Containment and intersection answers at a glance

target.evidence: modules/math/src/BoundingBox.cpp, BoundingSphere.cpp, BoundingFrustum.cpp; XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework assembly (decompiled, xna4-decomp; not a CNA file)

concepts.text: Plane: point/direction tests, normalisation, volume intersection and matrix or quaternion transform; the matrix transform is defective and only identity tests cover it.
Ray: box, sphere, plane and frustum intersection with tolerances that differ by shape; a zero direction is not a useful point query and Direction is not normalised by CNA.
tokens: Rays: one type, four intersection rules

concepts.text: BoundingBox: creation from points or sphere, merge, corners and containment/intersection; touching and empty-input behaviour follow each implementation and its exception type.
BoundingSphere: creation from points or box, merge, transform and containment/intersection; a non-uniform transform yields a conservative sphere, not an ellipsoid.
tokens: safe for broad-phase culling but loose

concepts.text: BoundingFrustum: matrix-derived planes and corners and containment/intersection; ray intersection classifies only the origin instead of computing an entry distance.

Plane::Transform(plane, matrix) inverts and then transposes in place through the alias-unsafe Matrix::Transpose; identity and diagonal scale hide the error, a translation or other non-symmetric inverse exposes it, and the quaternion overload is unaffected.
concepts.note: Published by B1 as CNA-BUG-001; stated as a plain scoped fact with a workaround.

concepts.text: BoundingFrustum::Intersects(Ray) classifies only the ray origin: outside gives no hit even when the ray enters the volume, inside gives 0, and only an origin exactly on a plane throws NotImplementedException; XNA 4.0 implements the full clip against six planes.
tokens: an origin exactly on a plane throws
concepts.note: Bible says the remaining branch throws as if common; it is reached only for an exact on-plane origin. XNA does not share the limitation (site errata 10; tutorial 44 repeats the 'exactly as in XNA' error). B1 CNA-BUG-004.

concepts.text: Ray/box, ray/plane and ray/sphere use different parallel and behind-origin tolerances (2^-24 slab test, 1e-5 plane parallel and behind limits, no epsilon for the sphere).
A zero-direction ray inside a box returns no hit (XNA returns 0); validate and normalise picking directions before querying several shapes.
concepts.note: XNA comparison added; issue WP04-i002.

BoundingSphere::Transform transforms the centre and scales the radius by the square root of the largest squared length of the matrix's three basis rows (XNA's formula).

concepts.text: The transformed sphere encloses the transformed ellipsoid: safe for broad-phase culling but looser than an ellipsoid or oriented bound.
Point is the integer coordinate pair; Rectangle adds bounds, containment, intersection/union, offset and inflation.
Rectangle's right and bottom edges are exclusive for point containment.
tokens: Left and top edges belong to the rectangle, right and bottom edges do not.

concepts.text: Rectangle::IsEmpty means X, Y, Width and Height are all zero; a zero-area rectangle elsewhere is not empty, so test Width > 0 && Height > 0 for area.

concepts.text: Color stores one packed UInt32 whose numeric form is AABBGGRR (R in bits 0-7), which on little-endian machines appears as R, G, B, A bytes.
concepts.note: Colour stores only the packed word; the byte channels are views of it, not separate storage.

concepts.text: The packed layout does not describe the polymorphic C++ object; renderer uploads must use the conversion paths, never reinterpret an array of Color.
tokens: Never reinterpret an array of Color as pixel bytes

concepts.text: Color::FromNonPremultiplied scales straight RGB by alpha for CNA's default premultiplied blending (BlendState::AlphaBlend = One / InverseSourceAlpha, SpriteBatch's default).
The integer FromNonPremultiplied(200, 80, 40, 128) yields (100, 40, 20, 128) by integer division; the float overload premultiplies and then uses the rounding constructor.
Color can hold either alpha convention; the selected BlendState determines how its channels are interpreted.
Named colour constants are generated API surface, not evidence about blend behaviour.
tokens: A named colour is API surface

concepts.text: MathHelper collects the angle constants, degree/radian conversion, clamping, interpolation, distance, angle wrapping and epsilon comparison.
MathHelper::Lerp is unclamped while SmoothStep clamps its amount before applying the cubic; the scalar and vector SmoothStep/Hermite/CatmullRom use different arithmetic from each other and from XNA.
concepts.note: Extended with the scalar/vector/XNA comparison; issue WP04-i014.

concepts.text: MachineEpsilonFloat is computed during dynamic initialisation (2^-24 by halving), so a static initialiser elsewhere calling WithinEpsilon may see 0; Decompose uses a separate FLT_EPSILON threshold.

concepts.text: Most low-level routines follow IEEE arithmetic instead of throwing: zero-vector normalisation, singular inversion, coincident look-at inputs and invalid projection ranges yield infinities or NaNs.

The validation policy is not uniform: the perspective builders validate distances and field of view (with an upper guard literal one float above MathHelper::Pi), while aspect ratio and the orthographic builders are not validated.
tokens: The aspect ratio and the orthographic builders are not validated at all.

concepts.text: Validate at the boundary where bad values could affect gameplay, content or a native API.
Curve evaluates an ordered CurveKeyCollection; keys hold position, value, incoming and outgoing tangents and Smooth or Step continuity.
CurveKeyCollection::Add inserts by ascending position (after equal positions).
tokens: inserts before the first key with a strictly greater position

concepts.text: ComputeTangents supports Flat, Linear and Smooth, for all keys and with separate in and out types.
Loop types before and after the key span: Constant clamps, Linear extrapolates, Cycle wraps, CycleOffset wraps with an accumulated value offset and Oscillate ping-pongs.
Tangents are per-segment quantities (value per segment, not per unit of position), which is why smooth tangents are scaled by the neighbouring spans.
concepts.note: TARGET extension.

concepts.text: Step evaluation compares the absolute query position with 1.0f instead of the segment's end, so Step segments away from [0,1] switch too early or too late (XNA switches at t >= 1).

issues.text: Vector2/3/4::Divide(v, s), operator/(v, s) and Matrix::Divide(m, s) divide each component by s, whereas XNA 4.0 multiplies by one reciprocal 1/s; Vector3::operator/= alone uses the reciprocal and its comment wrongly says Divide does too, so v / s, v /= s and XNA's v / s can differ in the last bit.
issues.evidence: modules/math/src/Vector2.cpp, Vector3.cpp, Vector4.cpp, Matrix.cpp (Divide, operator/=); XNA 4.0 IL (Vector3::Divide, op_Division, Matrix.Divide)

issues.text: Ray::Intersects(BoundingBox) returns no hit for a zero-direction ray whose origin is inside the box (XNA returns 0), uses a 2^-24 parallel threshold where XNA uses 1e-6, and divides where XNA multiplies by a reciprocal.
Ray::Intersects(BoundingSphere) treats only a strictly inside origin as a hit at 0 (XNA uses <=), so a ray starting exactly on the surface and pointing outward returns no hit in CNA and 0 in XNA.

Ray::ToString and BoundingBox::ToString emit literal doubled braces ({{Min:... }}) copied from FNA's string concatenation; XNA formats the same text with string.Format, which yields single braces. BoundingBoxTest.ToStringMatchesFNAFormat pins the FNA form, contrary to the project's XNA-over-FNA rule.

issues.text: Math ToString numbers use std::ostringstream defaults (six significant digits, C++ global locale) while XNA formats with Single.ToString(CurrentCulture); only Matrix::ToString's outer format was measured against XNA.

The FloatHash used by Vector2/3/4, Matrix, Quaternion (and CurveKey) hashes raw float bits, so values that compare equal (+0.0f vs -0.0f components) get different hash codes; .NET Single.GetHashCode returns 0 for both zeros, keeping XNA's hashes consistent with Equals.

issues.text: BoundingSphere::CreateFromBoundingBox computes (Min+Max)/2 and Distance(center, Max) where XNA computes Lerp(Min, Max, 0.5) and Distance(Min, Max)*0.5; last-bit agreement is unmeasured (the sphere oracle covers CreateFromPoints only).

MathHelper::SmoothStep/Hermite/CatmullRom (double, endpoint shortcuts) and the vector SmoothStep/Hermite (float Hermite basis) use different arithmetic from XNA's float Lerp(t^2(3-2t)) and Hermite forms; last-bit agreement is unmeasured and no oracle covers them.

MathHelper::MachineEpsilonFloat is a dynamically initialised static, so a static initialiser in another translation unit calling WithinEpsilon could observe 0; no such in-tree static consumer was found. Documentation caveat, recorded for completeness.
